integrity: The proof is analytic: it transforms the published first-order condition to a Gaussian Mills-ratio equation, proves strict invertibility by an integral identity, and derives both endpoint laws from controlled expansions. The bundled numerical checker is used only for regression.
scientific_limitations: The theorem refines only the inverse-Gaussian branch and gives endpoint asymptotics for the sharp parameter minimum. It does not classify the other distribution families treated in the motivating paper or assert that no equivalent older Mills-ratio formulation exists.
title: Universal Mills-ratio coordinates and endpoint laws for the inverse-Gaussian Chvátal minimum
